title: VMM-363 conducts hoist operations
description: U.S. Marines with Marine Medium Tiltrotor Squadron 363, Marine Aircraft Group 24, conduct hoist operations on Marine Corps Base Hawaii, January 24, 2019. The purpose of this training is to enhance evacuation capabilities of personnel utilizing the MV-22 Osprey in the event of a military or civilian mishap at sea. The ability to hoist stranded individuals from the water, via tiltrotor aircraft, provides another life- saving response option for Hawaii-based Marines and III Marine Expeditionary Force. (U.S. Marine Corps video by Lance Cpl. Eric Tso.)
keywords: 3rd Marine Regiment, MAGTF, III MEF, MAG-24, VMM-363, Hawaii, USMC

transcript.text: (MV-22 blades whirring)
- Today, the VMM-363 tried to further develop
our over-rudder hoist techniques.
The MV-22 has the ability to self deploy globally,
across continents, across oceans, and because
of our range and speed, other search and rescue assets
don't always have the ability to support us.
So we have a hoist on board the MV-22
and while we're not a search and rescue platform,
that's not a capability we were designed for,
we need the ability to have a self-rescue capability
as we fly across the Pacific or the Atlantic Ocean.
Today's training, and the training we've had
over the last couple weeks has been
to further develop that capability.
What profiles, what altitudes, what air speeds?
What do we do if we wanted to hoist somebody
or something out of the water during one of those
trans-Pacific or trans-Atlantic flights?
(MV-22 blades whirring)
We've validated some of our tactics, techniques,
and procedures in terms of how we're going to
approach a survivor at different altitudes.
Definitely, as the MV-22 came down to about 150 feet
over me, the water was choppy and rough and I had to
tread water to keep my head above the waves.
I think we had all the right things in place
from working with our United States Navy Search
and Rescue counterparts at HSM-37.
Overall, we learned a lot of great lessons today,
from how to hook up to the rescue strap
and then how to hoist into the bird itself.
(MV-22 blades whirring)
